---
title: "Time Series and Autoregressive Models — Review"
---

## Time Series

**Definition :** ordered sequence of observations $X(t_i) \in \mathbb{R}$

- **Lag** $\tau$ : shift between two observations — $X_{t-\tau}$ = Lagged Variable
- The **temporal order** carries information (≠ information theory)

**Basic statistics :** $\mathbb{E}[X]$ (mean), $\text{Var}[X]$ (variance), $\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]}$ (volatility)

---

## Possible Objectives

| Objective | Description |
|---|---|
| Identification | Trends, seasonalities, breaks |
| Explanation | How the past influences the present |
| Modelling | Formal representation of the process |
| Prediction | Anticipate future values |

::: {.callout-warning title="Trap"}
Good explanatory model ≠ good predictive model. Clarify the objective **before** choosing a model.
:::

---

## Stationarity

### Why it is necessary

- Consistency of relationships over time
- Reliable parameter estimation
- Simplified analysis
- Avoid spurious correlations (Spurious Results)

### Sources of non-stationarity

| Source | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Trend | Drifting mean | Rising asset price |
| Seasonality | Periodic variations | January effect, temperatures |
| Heteroskedasticity | Non-constant volatility | Markets in crisis |

### Formal definitions

**Strict Stationarity :**

$$
F(X_{t_1+\tau}, \ldots, X_{t_n+\tau}) = F(X_{t_1}, \ldots, X_{t_n}) \quad \forall\, \tau, n
$$

→ The entire joint distribution is invariant under time translation. Difficult to verify.

**Weak Stationarity — used in practice :**

$$
\text{a) } \mathbb{E}[X_t] = \mu = \text{cte} \quad \text{b) } \text{Cov}(X_t, X_{t+\tau}) = \gamma(\tau)
$$

→ Constant mean + autocovariance depending only on lag $\tau$.

### ADF Test (Augmented Dickey-Fuller)

- $H_0$ : unit root → **non-stationary**
- $H_1$ : **stationary**

| p-value | Decision |
|---|---|
| > 0.05 | Non-stationary — do not reject $H_0$ |
| ≤ 0.05 | Stationary — reject $H_0$ |

### How to make a series stationary

| Method | Formula / Action |
|---|---|
| Differencing | $\Delta X_t = X_t - X_{t-1}$ |
| Log returns | $r_t = \ln(X_t / X_{t-1})$ |
| Simple returns | $r_t = (X_t - X_{t-1})\,/\,X_{t-1}$ |
| Log transform | $\ln(X_t)$ — attenuates heteroskedasticity |
| Decomposition | Remove trend and seasonality |

::: {.callout-note title="Practical rule"}
**Prices → non-stationary** (p-value > 0.05) | **Returns → stationary** (p-value ≈ 0.00)

Systematically work with **returns** in finance.
:::

---

## Autocorrelation

### Definitions

**Correlation :**

$$
\text{Cor}(X, Y) = \frac{\text{Cov}(X,Y)}{\sqrt{\text{Var}(X)\,\text{Var}(Y)}}
$$

**Autocorrelation at lag $\tau$** (under stationarity) :

$$
\rho_\tau = \frac{\mathbb{E}[(X_t - \mu)(X_{t+\tau} - \mu)]}{\sigma^2}
$$

**ACF (Autocorrelation Function) :** $\text{ACF}(\tau) = \rho_\tau$ — represented by a correlogram.

### Reading the correlogram

| ACF signal | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| Slow, positive decay | Trend |
| Alternating +/− | Counter-trend / Mean-reversion |
| Peaks at regular intervals | Seasonality |
| All within CIs | White Noise |

**95 % Confidence Intervals (CI) :** $\pm\, 1.96\,/\,\sqrt{n}$

::: {.callout-tip title="Rule"}
Bar **exceeding** the CIs → **statistically significant** autocorrelation at this lag.
:::

## Autoregressive Models

### Three fundamental models

**AR(p) — Autoregressive of order p :**

$$
X_t = c + \sum_{i=1}^{p} \varphi_i\, X_{t-i} + \varepsilon_t
$$

**MA(q) — Moving Average of order q :**

$$
X_t = \mu + \varepsilon_t + \theta_1\,\varepsilon_{t-1} + \cdots + \theta_q\,\varepsilon_{t-q}
$$

**ARMA(p,q) :**

$$
X_t = c + \varepsilon_t + \sum_{i=1}^{p} \varphi_i\, X_{t-i} + \sum_{i=1}^{q} \theta_i\, \varepsilon_{t-i}
$$

### AR vs MA Comparison

| | AR(p) | MA(q) |
|---|---|---|
| Depends on | Past values $X_{t-i}$ | Past errors $\varepsilon_{t-i}$ |
| Memory | Infinite (if $|\varphi| < 1$) | Finite (exactly $q$ periods) |
| Estimation | Analytical for $p=1$ | Numerical (MLE) |

---

## AR(1) Model — Analytical Results

**Model :**

$$
X_t = c + \varphi_1\, X_{t-1} + \varepsilon_t, \quad \varepsilon_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\,\sigma_\varepsilon^2)
$$

### Key formulas

| Property | Formula | Key derivation |
|---|---|---|
| Mean | $\mu = c\,/\,(1-\varphi_1)$ | $\mathbb{E}[X_t] = \mathbb{E}[X_{t-1}]$ under stationarity |
| Variance | $\sigma^2 = \sigma_\varepsilon^2\,/\,(1-\varphi_1^2)$ | $\text{Var}[X_t] = \text{Var}[X_{t-1}]$ under stationarity |
| Autocorrelation lag 1 | $\rho_1 = \varphi_1$ | Independence of $X_t$ and $\varepsilon_{t+1}$ |
| Stationarity | $|\varphi_1| < 1$ | Necessary for $\sigma^2 > 0$ |

### Interpretation of $\varphi_1$

| Value of $\varphi_1$ | Behaviour | Application |
|---|---|---|
| $\varphi_1 > 0$ | Trending | Momentum strategies |
| $\varphi_1 < 0$ | Counter-trend (Mean-reverting) | Mean-reversion strategies |
| $\varphi_1 = 0$ | White noise | No predictability |
| $\varphi_1 = 1$ | Random walk | **Non-stationary** |
| $|\varphi_1| > 1$ | Explosive process | Invalid |

::: {.callout-warning title="Trap — Random walk"}
$\varphi_1 = 1$ → perfect **in-sample** fit, but **out-of-sample** prediction catastrophic.

**Good fit ≠ good predictive power.**
:::

---

## Order Selection (Model Order Selection)

### Information Criteria

$$
\text{AIC} = 2p - 2\ln(L) \qquad \text{BIC} = \ln(n)\cdot p - 2\ln(L)
$$

| Criterion | Penalty | Tendency | Usage |
|---|---|---|---|
| AIC | $2p$ | Higher orders | Prediction |
| BIC | $\ln(n)\cdot p$ | Lower orders | Identifying the true model |

**Rule :** **minimise** AIC or BIC. BIC stricter because $\ln(n) > 2$ if $n > 8$.

### Estimation for $p > 1$

- No analytical formula → **MLE** (Maximum Likelihood Estimation)

---

## Empirical Examples

| Series | ACF | $\varphi_1$ | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Random walk | Strong, all lags | ≈ 1 | Non-stationary, unpredictable |
| EUR/USD returns | Weak, CIs not exceeded | −0.125 | Efficient market |
| VIX returns | Significantly negative | < 0 | Mean-reversion of fear |
| S&P 500 returns | Weak | ≈ 0 | Little AR structure |
| Swiss GDP (quarterly) | Moderate | > 0 | Economic persistence |

---

## Pitfalls and Critical Points

::: {.callout-warning title="Do not forget"}

- **Prices ≠ stationary** — always work with returns in finance
- **Strict stationarity** ≠ weak stationarity — weak suffices in practice
- **ADF : p-value > 0.05** = non-stationary (reversed-sense trap)
- **AR(1), $|\varphi_1| \geq 1$** = non-stationary — the condition $|\varphi_1| < 1$ is imperative
- **Good in-sample fit** ≠ good out-of-sample prediction
- **ACF + BIC** → complementary tools for choosing order $p$

:::

---

## Relations between concepts

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A[Raw series] -->|ADF p>0.05| B[Non-stationary]
    B -->|Returns / Differences| C[Stationary series]
    C --> D[ACF]
    D -->|ρ₁ > 0| E[Trending AR\nφ₁ > 0]
    D -->|ρ₁ < 0| F[Counter-trend AR\nφ₁ < 0]
    D -->|Choice of p| G[AR p / AIC / BIC]
```
